title: Marcus Oyelaran — follow-up
notes_markdown:
### Update we gave

- 2 pilot sessions done (Oct 9 Priya Raman, Oct 13 Daniel Osei); both asked to keep using it
- Time to first confirmed suggestion: ~6 min (Priya), ~9 min (Daniel) into the writing task
- Bugs found and fixed: missing Claude chats (split export, ~140 chats), duplicate papers in suggestions
- Biggest asks: Notion + Granola import; meetings as sources ("half my ideas are said out loud")
- Berkeley conversations: 3 formal + ~9 informal since August

### Marcus's reaction

- Liked that we led with the failures; "two real sessions beat twenty demos"
- Still wants weekly usage: proposes a bar of **3 of the first 5 pilots using it weekly for 4 weeks** = "converted"
- Who pays: Daniel's grant-writing use case is interesting — postdocs with grants, and research-ops in labs
- Research-ops intro (from August) didn't pan out; he'll try someone else

### The ask

- Interested in a **$50k check into the pre-seed SAFE if the pilots convert**
- Would not lead; wants a lead or at least two other angels
- Wants: monthly 1-paragraph update; SAFE terms when ready (cap TBD with Surplus legal)

### Next steps

- [ ] Hudson — send SAFE terms summary + first monthly update (Nov 1)
- [ ] David — 3 more pilots by end of October (target 5 total)
- [ ] Hudson — weekly usage dashboard (opens/week per pilot) so "converted" is measurable
- [ ] Reconnect mid-November

transcript.text: What's the Notion mess?
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: Um, so, honestly — we don't have a Notion connector. He uploaded a zip, and our handling of it was bad. Titles had ids in them, his hierarchy got flattened.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: And he still wanted to keep using it.
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: Yeah. Because about nine minutes into the session it found the meeting note where his lab decided to pivot, and that was exactly what his grant paragraph was about.

transcript.text: Okay. That's a good story. What's the six?
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: Six?
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: You said nine minutes for him. You wrote six for her in the note you sent.
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: Oh, yeah. Priya, six minutes into the writing part, it found a Claude chat from March where she came up with the framing for her chapter.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: And what broke?
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: For Priya, we missed about a hundred forty of her Claude chats. Her export was split into two files and we only read one.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Ouch.
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: Fixed the same weekend. And duplicate papers. Same paper from Zotero and from Downloads, showing up twice. Also fixed, mostly.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: I like that you led with what broke. Most founders hide it until slide twenty.
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: We don't have slides.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Even better. Honestly, two real sessions beat twenty demos. What did they ask for?
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: Notion and Granola import, both from Daniel. And meetings as sources in general. He said "half my ideas are said out loud."
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: That's a great line.
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: Everyone gives us great lines. We need to build the things.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Ha. Okay. So, you know what I'm going to say.
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: Weekly usage.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Weekly usage. Here's what I'd like to see. Give me a bar. Five pilots. If three of them use it every week for four weeks, without you nagging, I'd call that converted.
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: Three of five, four weeks.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Three of five, four weeks. That's not a huge bar. But it's a real one.
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: That's fair. We can measure that. I'm building a little dashboard, opens per week per pilot.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Good. Who pays — did this change your thinking?
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: A little. Daniel was writing a grant. He has grant money. That's the first time the "who pays" thing felt concrete. Postdocs with grants.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: That's what I was saying in August. Postdocs and research-ops. The research-ops person I mentioned didn't work out, by the way, she changed jobs. I'll try someone else.
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: Thanks for trying.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Okay. So, here's where I am. If the pilots convert — your bar, three of five, four weeks — I'd be interested in putting fifty thousand into the pre-seed SAFE.
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: Oh. Wow. Okay.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: I won't lead. I'd want a lead, or at least two other angels in. And I'd want a monthly update, one paragraph, no fluff.
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: We can absolutely do that.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: What's the cap?
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: We're working it out with Surplus legal. I'll send terms when they're ready.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Fine. Don't rush it for me.
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: Can I ask — what would make you not do it? Like, other than the pilots not converting.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Honestly? If you start building for every request. Notion, Granola, Slack, lab spaces. You'll do twelve bad connectors. Pick the two that make the five pilots weekly users.
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: That's basically what David says every week.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: I say it, and then I want to build all of them.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Everyone does. Okay, I've got to run. Send me the first update November first.
transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran

transcript.text: November first. Thank you, Marcus.
transcript.speaker: Hudson Mitchell-Pullman

transcript.text: Thank you. Really.

transcript.text: Good luck. And David — how's the leave treating you?
